traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 304 records annotated as flowering (Jan 3, Feb 6, Mar 18, Apr 104, May 136, Jun 17, Jul 4, Sep 1, Oct 2, Nov 7, Dec 6); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, April and May. FEIS (Cytisus spp.) gives February to May in coastal British Columbia.

traits.fruiting_months.note: FEIS (Cytisus spp.): pods ripe in June and July (a general statement; one of its sources is the British Columbia study).

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Cytisus scoparius (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.64 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 3 records in 3 sources); trunks 0.63, branches 0.64. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: an invasive shrub of stiff, upright, green, ridged stems with tiny leaves, bright yellow pea flowers all along them in spring. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 2 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: green stems and tiny leaves; yellow flowers. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: flat pods 4 to 5 cm long, green ripening black. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: yellow flowers in April to June; pods green, black and bursting in July and August. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5): its petals, sepals, banner, wings and keel, stamens and pistil set from the characters of Fabaceae and Cytisus by the rules at the flowering plants. Its calyx by hand from the Flora of New Zealand (vol. IV, Webb and others 1988), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): about a quarter of the corolla's length, 2-lipped, so its sepals a third of a petal long and joined for most of it.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
